source.title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions

accepted.question_text: For the family of three-dimensional rational systems x_{n+1}=(α₁+β₁x_n+γ₁y_n+δ₁z_n)/(A₁+B₁x_n+C₁y_n+D₁z_n), y_{n+1}=(α₂+β₂x_n+γ₂y_n+δ₂z_n)/(A₂+B₂x_n+C₂y_n+D₂z_n), and z_{n+1}=(α₃+β₃x_n+γ₃y_n+δ₃z_n)/(A₃+B₃x_n+C₃y_n+D₃z_n) with nonnegative parameters and nonnegative initial conditions chosen so that all denominators remain positive, determine the global character of solutions for every special case. In particular, determine which special cases have bounded solutions, identify patterns of boundedness analogous to those found for two-dimensional rational systems, determine the global stability of equilibrium points and the periodic behavior for systems with bounded solutions, and for systems with unbounded solutions determine how the unboundedness occurs, describe the stable and unstable manifolds of equilibrium points, identify any invariants, and determine whether periodic trichotomies occur.

evidence.quote: Here we pose some open problems and conjectures on the global character of solutions of System (1). We wish to determine the boundedness characterization of each special case of System (1). ... We are especially interested in finding similar patterns of boundedness for System (1). For each system with bounded solutions we wish to determine the global stability character of their equilibrium points and the periodic nature of their solutions. For each system with unbounded solutions, we wish to determine the way that their solutions are unbounded, the stable and unstable manifolds of their equilibrium points, any invariants and whether there exists any periodic trichotomies.

accepted.question_text: Consider the 225 special cases arising from the three-dimensional rational system x_{n+1}=α₁/y_n, y_{n+1}=α₂/z_n, z_{n+1}=(α₃+β₃x_n+γ₃y_n+δ₃z_n)/(A₃+B₃x_n+C₃y_n+D₃z_n), where all parameters and initial conditions are nonnegative and all denominators remain positive. After eliminating x_n and y_n, this becomes the third-order rational difference equation z_{n+1}=(γ+α z_{n-1}+δ z_n z_{n-1}+α₁β z_{n-1} z_{n-2})/(C+A z_{n-1}+D z_n z_{n-1}+α₁B z_{n-1} z_{n-2}). For each of these 225 special cases, determine the boundedness character of solutions, their periodic behavior, and the global stability character of equilibrium points.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. Investigate the global character of solutions of the 225 special cases which are included in Eq. (5). For each special case, determine its boundedness character, its periodic behavior, and the global stability character of its equilibrium points.

accepted.question_text: Let α>0 and let k be a nonnegative integer. Does every positive solution of the higher-order rational difference equation α z_{n+1} = 1 + 1/(∏_{i=0}^{k} z_{n-i}) have a finite limit as n→∞?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. Every positive solution of the difference equation: αz n+1 = 1 + ∏ k i=0 z n−i has a finite limit.

accepted.question_text: Let α>0 and let k be a positive integer. Does every positive solution of the higher-order rational difference equation α z_{n+1} = 1 + 1/(∏_{i=1}^{k} z_{n-i}) converge to a periodic solution whose period divides k+3?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. Every positive solution of the difference equation: αz n+1 = 1 + ∏ k i=1 z n−i
converges to a (not necessarily prime) period (k + 3) solution.

accepted.question_text: Assume C>0. For the rational difference equation z_{n+1}=(α+β z_n+γ z_{n-1})/(A+B z_n+C z_{n-1}), if an equilibrium point z̄ is locally asymptotically stable, must that same equilibrium point be a global attractor of all positive solutions?

accepted.question_text: For the rational difference equation z_{n+1}=(α+β z_n)/(A+z_n+C z_{n-1}) with A≥0, all other parameters positive, and nonnegative initial conditions chosen so that denominators are never zero, does every solution converge?
